STEP 1 - Scene: A breakfast-style meal: scrambled eggs (or a white egg-based scramble) with crispy cooked bacon strips.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square white plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 26 x 26 x ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 575 cm^2, using a dinner-plate estimate of ~530 cm^2 for the usable circular area.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Scrambled eggs (pale, curdled white pieces, appear cooked without much added fat visible)
- Bacon, 2-3 cooked strips, browned and slightly glossy

STEP 4 - Area (percent of plate area):
- Scrambled egg: covers the upper-right central area, ~30%
- Bacon: lower-left diagonal strips, ~15%
- Total food coverage ~45% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume (using ~530 cm^2 as the plate area):
- Egg: 159 cm^2 x 2 cm = 318 ml
- Bacon: 80 cm^2 x 0.5 cm = 40 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Egg: 318 ml x 0.9 = ~286 g (scrambled egg is fairly dense but has air pockets; this is the bulk-density reduction)
- Bacon: 40 ml x 0.9 ≈ 36 g (cooked bacon pieces)

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Scrambled egg, cooked, no added fat: ~150 kcal/100 g → 286 g = ~429 kcal
- Cooked bacon, pan-fried: ~540 kcal/100 g → 36 g = ~194 kcal
- Total ≈ 620 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Roughly 320 g of food covering under half of a dinner plate, with eggs plus 2-3 bacon strips, is plausible for a breakfast plate. A typical 2-egg scramble with a few bacon strips falls in the 250–350 g range, so the estimate is consistent.

Total: ~320 g, ~620 kcal.
